clue.text: Superlatively fine art suffering

definitions.meaning: the most stylish or elegant, fine in the highest degree
in archaic grammar 'thou ...' means 'thou art suffering', from the verb smart, to feel pain

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition uses old second-person forms: 'thou art' is 'you are', and the verb 'smart' (to sting) takes the -est ending with 'thou'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means stylish or well dressed, so the superlative form describes the finest of all.

clue.text: Heads of Shell and Esso accompany identical oil producer

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, taken from each of the two company names

parts.note: identical means the same

explanation.surface: The bosses of two oil giants team up with a matching producer of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil producer' reads as a company like Shell or Esso, but it is a plant whose seeds are pressed for oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds yield a widely used cooking oil, so the plant is an oil producer.

clue.text: A smoker in Arbroath turned in by graduates

parts.note: lum is the Scots word for a chimney, something that smokes; Arbroath is a Scottish town

indicators.note: turned means the little word in is flipped round to read the other way

explanation.surface: Someone puffing away in a Scottish town is handed over to the police by former students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' suggests a person with a cigarette; here it is a chimney, LUM in Scots. 'turned' flips IN to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former students or graduates of a school or university.

clue.text: Shortcake mix on athlete's foot?

indicators.note: to mix is to stir ingredients together, so the letters of the biscuit's name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A baking recipe for shortcake applied to a fungal foot infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'athlete's foot' looks like the skin complaint; the question mark signals the literal reading, a shoe worn on a runner's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked running shoe is what an athlete wears on the foot, punning on the infection.

clue.text: Shippers heed order for food

indicators.note: to put into order is to arrange, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Freight companies are told to pay attention to an instruction about catering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a command to heed, but it signals rearranging SHIPPERS and HEED. Shepherd's pie is a British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's pie is a baked dish of minced meat under mashed potato, an example of food.

clue.text: Burns doesn't do any work on book

indicators.note: on places the idling word after the book abbreviation, attached to it

parts.note: to laze is to idle about doing nothing

explanation.surface: A remark that the poet Robert Burns idles rather than writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' poses as the Scottish poet; with the capital explained away, it is the verb meaning flames.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze is to burn fiercely, so blazes is a synonym of burns as a verb.

clue.text: Redhead has number left over

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the whole run of letters the other way round

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person has one figure remaining unused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'left over', meaning remaining, but it reverses NINEL to give the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolshevik Reds, so he was head of the Reds in a cryptic reading of redhead.

clue.text: From America to Australia, revolutionary modern technology producing garb of the 1940s

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America
taken as written
Oz is a slang name for Australia
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: Ground-breaking tech crossing from the USA to Australia creates clothing from wartime years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' seems to praise the technology, but it turns round the travel phrase; 'From' and 'producing' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoot suit, with baggy trousers and a long jacket, was a flamboyant fashion of the 1940s.

clue.text: Logo said to represent herbaceous plant

indicators.note: here the letters are made to stand for something new by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A company emblem is said to stand for a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' reads as a link meaning 'claimed', but it is part of the fodder with LOGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidago is the botanical genus of goldenrod, a herbaceous perennial plant.

clue.text: Singular health centre surrounded by singular grass

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: surrounded by means the central piece sits inside the strange word

parts.note: singular can mean odd or strange, which is queer

indicators.note: the centre of the word health is its inner letters, here EAL

explanation.surface: A lone spa sits in a field of odd grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'health centre' reads as a clinic but gives EAL, the middle of HEALTH. 'grass' looks like lawn; it is the verb's noun, an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for an informer, and so is a squealer, one who tells on others.

clue.text: Remarkable Scots look round or square

parts.note: unco is a Scots word meaning remarkable or extraordinary

indicators.note: round tells us to turn the little word for look the other way

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A question of whether an impressive Scottish appearance is circular or boxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round or square' looks like a choice of shapes; 'round' reverses LO and 'square' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Square is slang for old-fashioned and unhip, which is what uncool means.

clue.text: Significant development as holiday finished

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
through means finished, as in 'I'm through with it'

explanation.surface: Something big happened just as the vacation ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakthrough is an important advance or discovery, a significant development.

clue.text: Soviet leader in coat no longer politically correct in Belarus

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the fur coat

parts.note: a mink fur coat is now frowned upon by many

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Soviet boss wears a fur coat that would now be thought unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soviet leader' suggests Lenin or Stalin; it just gives S, put inside MINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Minsk is the capital city of Belarus, so it is a place found within that country.

clue.text: Tough, shrewd and practical hands rode range

indicators.note: to range is to roam freely, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Farm workers rode across the open range, a hardy, practical lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like the open grassland the hands rode over, but it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-nosed describes someone tough-minded and unsentimental, realistic in dealings.

clue.text: There's parliament — there's no substitute

parts.note: taken as written, with the 's treated as a joining word
the Althing is the parliament of Iceland, one of the oldest in the world

explanation.surface: A claim that parliament is the genuine article that cannot be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The parliament is Iceland's Althing, a word few solvers expect.
explanation.definitionFit: The real thing is the genuine article, something for which no replacement will do.

clue.text: To love, seek the love of one who's qualified for business in Queensland

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
to woo is to court someone
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration, a business qualification

explanation.surface: A romantic plea to court someone with a business degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business' seems to go with 'Queensland', but it belongs to the MBA; 'love' gives both O and, by courting, WOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toowoomba is a city in south-east Queensland, Australia, a place within that state.

clue.text: Bird, in a manner of speaking, joining other ranks

parts.note: an accent is a way of pronouncing words
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, those who are not officers

explanation.surface: A soldier, figuratively speaking, joins the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' reads as 'so to speak'; the 'in' is a link and the rest gives ACCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The accentor is a small songbird; the dunnock or hedge sparrow is one.

clue.text: Nick has to stop work

definitions.meaning: to nick is British slang for to steal
to finish work for the day

explanation.definitionFit: Knock off is slang both for stealing something and for finishing work.

clue.text: Talk for a change about empty apartment

indicators.note: about means the change wraps round the emptied flat

parts.note: a conversion is a change from one form to another

indicators.note: empty leaves only the outside letters of the word apartment

explanation.surface: A plan to talk about remodelling a vacant flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty apartment' reads as a vacant flat, but 'empty' strips the word to its first and last letters, which 'about' places inside the change.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is an exchange of talk between people.

clue.text: One man in a boat looking up old address

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: Harris is one of the three men in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: A lone sailor gazes skyward towards an old house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old address' reads as a former home; it is an old form of addressing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirrah is an archaic form of address to a man or boy, often contemptuous.

clue.text: Was an offender heard in a province of Pakistan?

indicators.note: heard means the province's name is spoken and a word of the same sound is written

parts.note: Sind, also spelt Sindh, is a province in southern Pakistan

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone heard in a Pakistani region broke the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to commit an offence against moral law, so one who sinned was an offender.

clue.text: A strange device is better than one with nothing right

parts.note: to excel is to outdo or surpass
one is the Roman numeral I
nothing is zero, written as O

explanation.surface: An odd gadget outperforms one with nothing on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's poem 'Excelsior' has a youth bearing a banner 'with the strange device, Excelsior!'
explanation.definitionFit: In Longfellow's poem the banner carried the strange device Excelsior, so the clue quotes it.

clue.text: Don't touch and go

definitions.meaning: depart, as in leaving a room

explanation.definitionFit: Leave means both to let something be untouched and to depart.

clue.text: Antelope discovered by Maori biologist

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered inside the following words, the run sitting across them

explanation.surface: A New Zealand scientist finds a new species of antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered by' looks like a scientific find; the antelope sits inside MaORI BIologist.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope.

clue.text: Hard worker — one familiar with long-term investment?

definitions.meaning: someone who works like a ..., very diligently
investment is the old word for a siege; the people of Troy endured a ten-year siege

explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is to work tirelessly, and Troy's citizens knew a long siege well.

clue.text: Pacifier to go on trial

parts.note: a dummy is the British name for a baby's pacifier
a run is a go or attempt

explanation.surface: A baby's comforter is put in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on trial' looks like a court case; 'on' is a link and 'trial' the definition, a practice run.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a rehearsal or test, a trial before the real thing.

clue.text: Action not premeditated by arbitrator going to law

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, settles disputes in sport
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: An impulsive act by a mediator turning to the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an involuntary response, an action done without thinking ahead.

clue.text: Slough keeps articles enclosed

indicators.note: keeps means the casting-off word holds the two articles within it

parts.note: to slough is to cast off, as a snake sheds its skin
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An English town in Berkshire stores some items under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' poses as the Berkshire town, but it is the verb meaning cast off, SHED, holding A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathed means encased in a covering, as a sword in its scabbard, so enclosed.
